title: Lena and the Flying Trials
markdown:
The sun cracked the horizon like a golden egg, spilling pink and peach across the sky. Lena Bright bounced out of bed. Today was the Hawk Academy flying trials. Her heart thumped like a hummingbird’s wings. Outside, birds chirped a zippy tune. The morning air tasted crisp, like a juicy apple. Upstairs, sizzling bacon and sweet berries made her tummy rumble.

Then a shiver. Not from cold. From doubt. Torque, her robot hawk, was fast. A marvel. But Jasper Swift’s hawk, Bolt, was faster than a dragonfly. Lena gripped her lucky falconry glove. “Today,” she whispered to her reflection, “I have to be brave. Truly, deeply brave.”

At the training grounds, energy crackled. Apprentices preened their real falcons. Lena, with quick practiced moves, clipped Torque’s sleek harness. His metallic eyes blinked blue. “Ready, Torque?” she chirped. He whirred a happy hum, and her nerves settled a fraction.

They launched. Torque became a blur of chrome and power against the vast blue. Lena felt a thrilling surge as they soared higher. Suddenly, a jarring hiccup. Torque’s tracker, a tiny blinking dot on her wrist, sputtered. Then it went dark. “What?” Lena gasped. Torque’s speed, his distance, gone. A cold knot tightened in her stomach. This was no glitch.

“Someone’s jamming them!” a voice yelled. Chaos. Apprentices scrambled. Falcons agitated. Trackers flickered like broken lights. The whole competition was sabotaged. Lena’s sharp gaze locked onto Jasper Swift. He stood apart, a smug knowing smirk on his face. Bolt, his falcon, seemed totally fine.

The familiar fear of not being good enough tried to creep back. Lena looked at Torque, his powerful form still breathtaking. He trusted her. She had to trust him, and herself. “We won’t quit, Torque,” she declared, her voice firm. “We’ll figure this out.”

They swooshed, Lena’s eyes scanning the ground. A faint metallic glint near thick tangled bushes. No bird would land there. “There!” she cried. They swooped down. Lena dismounted, boots crunching on leaves. Beneath a gnarled branch, a small box pulsed with an annoying buzz. A jammer.

“Pro tip from someone who learned the hard way,” Lena muttered, picking up the cool metal, “sabotage usually leaves a trace.” Jasper. He wanted everyone else out. “Come on, Torque. We need to catch him before he ruins everything.”

They rocketed skyward. Jasper and Bolt were just ahead. Jasper glanced back, eyes widening. He had not expected her to find the jammer so fast. He pushed Bolt harder, a desperate burst of speed.

Jasper pulled a sly move. He signaled Bolt to dive sharply toward a tricky narrow canyon, a dangerous shortcut Lena usually avoided. A clear test. A tempting trap. If Lena followed, she risked a crash. If she didn’t, Jasper would win.

Lena hesitated. Her stomach lurched. She pictured Bolt zipping through the canyon, Torque stuck behind, victory slipping away. She saw Torque’s trust in his bright blue eyes. She felt the weight of the jammer in her glove. Was winning worth sacrificing her integrity? “No,” Lena said, her voice strong and clear. “Not like this.” She steered Torque away from the canyon, choosing the longer, safer, honest route. It felt like losing, but her gut screamed it was right. Jasper zipped through the canyon, a brown streak. He reappeared far ahead. Lena’s heart sank, but she kept Torque flying true.

They approached the finish line. Jasper was already there, Bolt perched triumphantly. The judges huddled. Bolt’s tracker had worked perfectly. Then a booming announcement cut through the field. “A device has been found. A jamming device. Originating from the vicinity of Jasper Swift.”

Jasper paled. His smug smirk vanished. “It wasn’t me!”

Lena landed Torque gently. She held up the buzzing jammer. “This was found near your usual practice spot. And your falcon’s tracker never faltered.” She looked at Jasper not with anger, but with pity. He had been so focused on winning he had forgotten how to fly with honor.

The judges conferred. Jasper Swift was disqualified. Lena Bright and Torque crossed the line, and Torque’s tracker, as if it had been waiting for honest air, blinked awake again and proved their speed and skill.

Lena beamed. Torque whirred happily, his wings giving a triumphant flap. She had not only won the trials. She had refused the canyon. That was the bravery she had asked of her reflection at dawn.

She and Torque took to the skies again, the same pink morning still spilling across the horizon, their partnership steadier than any tracker.
characters: Lena (an apprentice falconer), Torque (a training robot hawk)
